svg.text: Codex Low-Token Two-Stage Development Workflow
Use the strong web model for reasoning-heavy development; reserve local Codex for real execution and verification.
1. Input to the Web Stage
Project ZIP + Web Skill + requirement
Only give the web model its own Skill. Do not upload the Local Codex Skill here.
2. Web Reasoning Stage — do the expensive thinking once
• Understand architecture and requirements
• Create plan.md for non-trivial work
• Implement the primary code changes
• Perform static code review
• Produce minimal patch ZIP
• List required deletions
• Write a complete Local Codex handoff
• Mark what still requires runtime verification
Avoid by default: full compile/test loops, local SDK setup, unrelated refactors.
3. Handoff Boundary
Apply the minimal patch locally → pass Local Skill + Web handoff prompt to Codex.
Deletion commands live in the handoff because an overlay ZIP cannot reliably express file deletion.
4. Local Codex Stage — execute, verify, repair narrowly
Delete specified files → build/compile → relevant tests → smoke/runtime checks → small fixes → re-verify → cleanup
Do not redo requirement analysis or architecture design. Escalate architecture-level failures back to the Web stage.
Token-saving idea: prevent duplicate reasoning and duplicate primary implementation on Local Codex.
